title: Arts, sayings and a long conversation
goal: Round off the module with a long conversation that brings together everything you've learned, plus Sundanese arts and the sayings you'll hear for as long as you live in West Java.
bekal: Sundanese arts: wayang golek, angklung, degung, pencak silat
a long conversation without a side-by-side translation

dialogs.title: Paguneman — One last evening on the porch
dialogs.intro: Six months after Rani arrived. Saturday night, the rain has eased, bandrek (hot ginger drink) in hand. Bu Imas, Sari and Rani sit on the porch. This is the module's closing conversation, and everything you've learned is in it.

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Teu karaos nya, Néng. Tos genep sasih di dieu.
lines.id: Time flies, doesn't it, Néng? Six months here already.
lines.literal: not felt [nya], Néng. already six month at here.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Muhun, Bu. Karaosna mah nembé kamari abdi sumping nyeret koper.
lines.id: Yes, ma'am. It feels like only yesterday I arrived dragging my suitcase.
lines.literal: yes, Bu. feeling-its [mah] just yesterday I come drag suitcase.

lines.speaker: Sari:
lines.text: Ayeuna mah tos tiasa nawar di pasar, tos tiasa ngambek maké basa Sunda.
lines.id: Now she can haggle at the market and even sulk in Sundanese.
lines.literal: now [mah] already can bargain at market, already can sulk using language Sundanese.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Ih, kaduhung nyarioskeun éta ka manéh.
lines.id: Hey, I regret telling you that.
lines.literal: hey, regret telling that to you.

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Hahaha. Tapi leres, Néng. Basa téh kudu dipaké, ulah diapalkeun waé.
lines.id: Hahaha. But it's true, Néng. A language has to be used, not just memorized.
lines.literal: hahaha. but true, Néng. language [téh] must be-used, don't be-memorized only.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Aya hiji nu masih hésé, Bu: undak usuk. Sok sieun lepat kénéh.
lines.id: There's one thing that's still hard, ma'am: undak usuk (speech levels). I'm still often afraid of getting it wrong.
lines.literal: there-is one that still hard, Bu: undak usuk. often afraid wrong still.

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Sing sabar. Urang Sunda ogé loba nu can pati apal. Nu penting niatna.
lines.id: Be patient. Plenty of Sundanese people haven't fully mastered it either. What matters is the intention.
lines.literal: may patient. people Sundanese also many that not-yet too memorized. that important intention-the.

lines.speaker: Sari:
lines.text: Aya paribasa: cikaracak ninggang batu, laun-laun jadi legok.
lines.id: There's a saying: drops of water falling on a stone slowly wear a hollow in it.
lines.literal: there-is saying: drip water fall-on stone, slowly-slowly become hollow.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Hartina sagala hal kudu ku sabar, nya?
lines.literal: meaning-its every thing must with patience, [nya]?

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Leres pisan. Sanaos leutik, upami terus-terusan mah tangtos aya hasilna.
lines.id: Exactly. Even if it's small, if you keep at it, there will be results.
lines.literal: true very. although small, if continuous [mah] certainly there-is result-its.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Bu, upami taun payun abdi ngalih ka Jakarta deui… abdi bakal kangen.
lines.id: Ma'am, if I move back to Jakarta next year… I'll miss you.
lines.literal: Bu, if year next I move to Jakarta again… I will miss.

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Ulah dipikiran ti ayeuna atuh. Nu penting ayeuna urang di dieu.
lines.id: Don't think about that now. What matters is we're here now.
lines.literal: don't be-thought from now [atuh]. that important now we at here.

lines.speaker: Sari:
lines.text: Jeung ulah poho: sakali jadi urang Bandung, salawasna jadi urang Bandung.
lines.id: And don't forget: once a Bandung person, always a Bandung person.
lines.literal: and don't forget: once become person Bandung, forever become person Bandung.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Hatur nuhun pisan, Bu, Sar. Kanggo sadayana.
lines.id: Thank you so much, ma'am, Sar. For everything.
lines.literal: thank you very, Bu, Sar. for everything.

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Sami-sami, Néng. Mangga, bandrékna diraosan, tiris.
lines.id: You're welcome, Néng. Here, drink your bandrek before it gets cold.
lines.literal: same-same, Néng. please, bandrek-the be-tasted, cold.

notes: **Sasih** = month (high lemes); loma and ordinary lemes: **bulan**. It appears in invitations and formal writing.
**Nyarioskeun** = to tell, recount (lemes); loma: **nyaritakeun**. Notice the *N-* + base + *-keun* pattern you've known since Unit 10.
**Sanaos** = although (lemes); loma: **sanajan** or **najan**. It pairs with *tapi* (but) or *tetep* (still).
**Kénéh** = still (loma); the lemes is **kénging** or, more commonly, **masih**. *Sieun lepat kénéh* = still afraid of getting it wrong.
**Kangen** (to miss) is borrowed from Indonesian. The more native Sundanese word: **sono**. *Abdi sono ka Bandung* = I miss Bandung.

**Terus-terusan** = continuously. Doubling words like this is very productive in Sundanese: *laun-laun* (little by little), *isuk-isuk* (early in the morning), *sakali-kali* (once in a while), *rada-rada* (somewhat).

grammars.title: Ten sayings you'll hear
body: Paribasa (sayings) are alive in everyday Sundanese conversation, not just in textbooks. These ten are the most quoted: in speeches, in chats, even on banners.

head: Paribasa
Literally
Meaning
rows: love, sharpen and nurture one another
the Sundanese principle of living together
dripping water on a stone slowly makes a hollow
small, steady effort always pays off
*Ka cai jadi saleuwi, ka darat jadi salebak.*
in the water, one pool; on land, one valley
together through thick and thin, of one mind
good in both words and behavior
don't cut a shirt as tight as your own body
don't judge others by your own measure
speech must be measured, words must be weighed
bent and stooped, still gathered together
togetherness in good times and bad
take time as your mother, the age as your father
family is family, even when they're wrong
dig up lesser galangal while staying alert

after: The first, **silih asih, silih asah, silih asuh**, is the most important to recognize. It's written on government offices, schools and banners all over West Java, and is often called a summary of the whole Sundanese philosophy of life.

You don't need to use them in conversation; a newcomer quoting paribasa can sound forced. What's useful is **recognizing** them when you hear them, because people often use one to wrap up a discussion, and missing its meaning means missing the point.

head: Art form
What it is
Note
rows: the clown servant *Cepot* speaks funny loma
UNESCO-recognized in 2010; one person, one note
softer and slower than Javanese gamelan
created by Gugum Gumbira in the 1970s
struck bamboo, a cousin of the angklung
lion figures carried in a parade
long tale told to zither music

blocks.text: ⚠️ If you only have time for one thing, watch **wayang golek by Asep Sunandar Sunarya**. There are hours of recordings free on YouTube, and they teach undak usuk better than any chapter in this module: the knights speak high lemes, Cepot answers in cheeky loma, and the whole audience knows exactly when a line has been crossed. It's the speech-level system performed, not explained.

blocks.title: Folk tales worth knowing
items: **Sangkuriang** — how the Tangkuban Parahu volcano came to be; the tale of a son who unknowingly falls in love with his mother.
**Lutung Kasarung** — Princess Purbasari and a god in the form of a black monkey; the most famous Sundanese pantun.
**Ciung Wanara** — a prince cast out as a baby who returns to win back the throne of Galuh.
**Mundinglaya Dikusumah** — the quest for the *Layang Salaka Domas*.
**Nyi Roro Kidul** — queen of the Southern Sea, a legend all along Java's south coast.

blocks.text: Read this conversation **without** flipping back for translations. Every word in it has already appeared in this module. If you can follow it, you've completed A1.

blocks.title: Two neighbors meet at the corner shop
items: **A:** Punten, Bu Éha. Badé ka mana isuk-isuk kieu?
**B:** Ieu badé ka pasar heula. Ari Néng?
**A:** Abdi mah badé ka kantor. Tapi angkotna teu acan aya.
**B:** Ari ka kantor téh naék naon biasana?
**A:** Angkot héjo, terus ngalih di alun-alun. Kirang langkung tilu puluh menit.
**B:** Wah, tebih ogé nya. Tara telat?
**A:** Sok telat upami macét. Mindeng abdi indit tabuh genep supados aman.
**B:** Sing sabar atuh. Bandung mah macétna beuki parah.
**A:** Muhun, Bu. Punten, angkotna sumping. Abdi ti payun nya.
**B:** Mangga, ati-ati di jalan. Sing lancar sadayana.

blocks.text: If a sentence or two isn't clear yet, that's normal and not a sign of failure. Go back to the unit that covers it: question words in Unit 9, time markers in Unit 14, directions and angkots in Unit 11, the particles *mah* and *téh* in Unit 8.

blocks.title: Ten closing phrases worth keeping for life
items: **Punten.** — Excuse me. The word that opens everything.
**Mangga.** — Please, go ahead. The answer to everything.
**Hatur nuhun.** — Thank you.
**Sami-sami.** — You're welcome.
**Kumaha damang?** — How are you?
**Abdi nembé diajar basa Sunda.** — I've only just started learning Sundanese.
**Hapunten upami abdi lepat.** — Sorry if I've made a mistake.
**Duka teuing.** — I have no idea.
**Mugia énggal damang.** — Get well soon.
**Wilujeng, sing sae salamina.** — Congratulations, may it always go well.
